user.title: Add a DDP pixel controller
user.description: Enter the controller's address. Home Assistant asks the controller for its output layout and checks which kind of controller it is. If it can't tell, you'll describe the outputs yourself. DDP has no acknowledgement, so setup can only check that a socket opens. Nothing is sent to the lights.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the controller (UDP port 4048).

controller.title: Controller type
controller.description: Detected controller: {detected}. A vendor controller type adds a controller device with a main light (on/off and brightness) for the controller's built-in effects and presets, a light per palette color and a Scene select. Every type then defines its DDP outputs on the next steps, prefilled from the layout the controller reports; Generic DDP creates only those per-output DDP lights.

data_description.controller_type: Choose Generic DDP if the detected type is wrong or you only want the DDP lights.

manual.title: Describe the outputs
manual.description: Define the outputs; the fields are prefilled from the detected or stored layout when there is one. Next you'll enter each output's name and pixel range; one light is created per output. For a vendor controller type, keep the ranges in line with the controller's own port setup: the controller maps the DDP channels to its ports.

data_description.data_type: Channels per pixel: RGB is 3, RGBW is 4.
data_description.outputs: How many Home Assistant lights to create, 1 to 16. Each covers a pixel range you enter next, so this is not the pixel count: a 122-pixel strip on two ports is 2 outputs. The pixel count follows from the highest last pixel.

output.title: Output {output} of {outputs}
output.description: Name this output and the pixels it covers, counting from 1 across the whole controller. Ranges may leave gaps but must not overlap another output. For a vendor controller type, the ranges should normally match the controller's own port setup, since the controller maps DDP channels to its ports.

data_description.name: The light's name.
data_description.first_pixel: First pixel of this output, counting from 1.
data_description.last_pixel: Last pixel of this output, included.
data_description.reversed: The controller reverses this output, so its pixel lights count from the other end: Light 1 is the last pixel of the range. It does not change what DDP sends. Prefilled from the controller's layout when it reports one; set it by hand for a Generic DDP controller that reverses the port.

reconfigure.title: Reconfigure the controller
reconfigure.description: Detected controller: {detected}. Stored pixel type: {data_type}. Layout the controller reports now: {layout}. Submitting continues to the output steps, prefilled from the layout the controller reports now (pixel type and outputs, keeping the names and Reversed flags you stored), so a change of the controller's input mode (3 or 4 channels) takes effect; an output that is gone loses its light. Generic DDP, or a controller that reports no layout (none), prefills them with the stored outputs. Changing the host keeps the device and its lights. Changing the type adds or removes the controller device and its entities; the DDP lights are kept.

data_description.host: IP address or hostname of the controller (UDP port 4048).
data_description.controller_type: Generic DDP creates only the per-output DDP lights.

error.cannot_connect: Could not open a UDP socket to the controller. Check the host.
error.invalid_config: The host or pixel count is not valid for DDP.
error.invalid_range: The last pixel must not come before the first pixel.
error.output_overlap: This range overlaps an earlier output.

data_description.brightness_cap: Maximum output as a percent of full. Every frame is capped, including effects.
data_description.color_order: Channel order the pixels expect on the wire.
data_description.fps: Frames per second for animated effects.
data_description.keepalive: Re-send the current frame this often, in seconds, so the controller doesn't fall back to its built-in effect (the NDB-Pro does after about 20 s without DDP). 0 turns it off; otherwise at least 0.5.
data_description.pixel_lights: Add a light for every pixel of every output ("Output 1 Light 1" and so on, counted from the start of the installed string), next to the output lights, to turn single pixels on and off and color them. A 122-pixel controller gets 122 more lights. Turning it off removes them.

controller_failed.message: Could not command the controller for {entity}: {error}

socket_failed.message: Cannot open a DDP socket to {host}: {error}

unknown_controller_type.message: Unknown controller type {type}. Reconfigure the entry or upgrade the integration.

controller_unreachable.message: The controller at {host} did not answer: {error}

not_a_ddp_light.message: {entity} is not a DDP light; set_pattern works only on a DDP output light or All outputs.

effect_without_colors.message: Effect {effect} takes no colors, so it cannot show a pattern. Effects that can: {effects}

rgbw_needs_rgbw_pixels.message: {entity} drives RGB pixels, so pattern colors take red, green, blue only. To use white, switch the controller to a 4-channel input mode and reconfigure the entry.

rgbw_effect_unsupported.message: Effect {effect} renders RGB only, so its colors take red, green, blue only. Effects that take white: {effects}

not_a_controller.message: {entity} is not the controller light; recall_preset works only on the light named like the controller device.

palette_not_a_controller.message: {entity} is not the controller light; set_colors works only on the light named like the controller device.

pixel_light_pattern.message: {entity} is a single pixel, so it shows one color; set_pattern works only on a DDP output light or All outputs.

recall_preset.name: Recall preset
recall_preset.description: Plays one of the controller's 20 stored show presets (1-10 are Show 1, 11-20 Show 2). DDP segment lights are turned off so the controller's scene shows.

set_pattern.name: Set pattern
set_pattern.description: Shows a repeating pattern of colors on a DDP light, rendered by an effect (palette by default: fixed blocks of the colors). The pattern is kept across restarts; a later color replaces it.

colors.name: Colors
colors.description: 1 to 16 colors, each a list of red, green, blue from 0 to 255, for example [[255, 0, 0], [0, 255, 0]]. On RGBW pixels a color may add white as a fourth value, for example [255, 0, 0, 0] or [0, 0, 0, 255], with effects that take white (palette).

block_size.name: Block size
block_size.description: Pixels per color block. 1 with two colors is every other pixel. Only effects with blocks (palette) take it.

effect.name: Effect
effect.description: The effect that renders the colors. Effects that take a single color use the first one.

params.name: Effect parameters
params.description: Other parameters of the effect as a mapping, for example speed: 4 for chase.

brightness.name: Brightness
brightness.description: Brightness from 1 to 255. Leave empty to keep the light's brightness.

set_colors.name: Set colors
set_colors.description: Sets the colors the controller's built-in effects use (its palette of 5 custom colors), on the controller light. The controller need not be on, and DDP lights keep the pixels. No colors clears the palette, so the controller picks random colors.

colors.name: Colors
colors.description: 0 to 5 colors for palette slots 1 to 5; the remaining slots are emptied. Each is a list of red, green, blue from 0 to 255, or cool_white or warm_white for the controller's white LEDs, for example ["warm_white", [255, 0, 0]]. An empty list clears the palette, so the controller picks random colors.

background.name: Background
background.description: The background color as red, green, blue from 0 to 255, for effects that use one. Leave empty to keep it.
